findings.title: Table 3 novelty (TM-score to nearest PDB protein) is not computed anywhere in the repo
findings.quote: novelty is the average TM-score (Zhang & Skolnick, 2005) of each sample to its most similar protein in PDB.
findings.claim: The NOV. column of Table 3 (e.g. Multiflow 0.61) is defined as the average TM-score of each designable sample to its most similar PDB protein; the repo computes diversity via FoldSeek clustering (experiments/utils.py:75-104) and PMPNN consistency/designability, but contains no PDB-search / TM-score / novelty computation.
findings.concern: A whole column of the headline results table (novelty for every method) has no code path that produces it, so those numbers cannot be reproduced or checked from this repo.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add or point to the script that searches each designable sample against PDB and computes the TM-score novelty reported in Table 3 (and Fig. 3-adjacent analyses).

findings.title: Text8 DFM experiment (Fig. 2, Table 5) has no code in this repository
findings.quote: Table 5. Model log-likelihoods computed on the test set of text8 in bits-per-character (BPC).
findings.claim: Section 6.1 / App. I report the DFM-vs-D3PM/SEDD text8 study: Fig. 2 (NLL-vs-entropy Pareto frontier, GPT-J-6B evaluation) and Table 5 (log-likelihood in BPC, 86M-param character transformer). A recursive grep of the repo (excluding openfold/ProteinMPNN) for text8|d3pm|sedd|gpt-?j|bpc|character finds no matching source; this repo is protein-only.
findings.concern: The paper's first contribution (DFMs outperform discrete-diffusion baselines) is validated only by the text8 experiment, and none of that experiment's code (data prep, training, NLL/entropy evaluation, BPC bound) ships in the audited artefact — Fig. 2 and Table 5 are not reproducible from here.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm whether the text8 code lives in the linked repo (andrew-cr/discrete_flow_models) and, if so, add a pointer / commit hash for the exact Fig. 2 / Table 5 scripts; otherwise release them.

findings.title: Reported dispersion stats (Table 4 std, Table 6 SEM, 3-seed averaging) not produced by any script
findings.claim: The metric aggregators compute only means (e.g. compute_inverse_folding_metrics / compute_forward_folding_metrics use .mean(); a grep for .std()/.sem()/stderr over multiflow/ finds no dispersion computation). Yet Table 4 reports 'mean ± std' (2.2 ± 2.6, 15.3 ± 4.5), Table 3 is 'the average of three seeds', and Table 6 reports standard error.
findings.concern: The uncertainty numbers (std / standard error) and the three-seed averaging that the paper reports are not produced by any released code, so a reader cannot regenerate the ± values or the multi-seed aggregation from the repo.
findings.resolution: Authors: add the script that aggregates per-sample bb_rmsd into std (Table 4) and runs/averages the three seeds with standard error (Tables 3/6), or document the exact off-repo procedure.
findings.paper_ref: Table 4 caption 'mean ± std'; Sec 6.2.1 'average of three seeds ... Table 6 ... standard error'

findings.title: Released synthetic distillation set has 6550 examples, not the paper's stated 4179
findings.quote:
if self._dataset_cfg.use_synthetic:
    self.synthetic_csv = pd.read_csv(self._dataset_cfg.synthetic_csv_path)
    self._synthetic_pdb_to_cluster = _read_clusters(self._dataset_cfg.synthetic_cluster_path, synthetic=True)

    # offset all the cluster numbers by the number of real data clusters
    num_real_clusters = metadata_csv['cluster'].max() + 1
    def synthetic_cluster_lookup(pdb):
        pdb = pdb.upper()
        if pdb not in self._synthetic_pdb_to_cluster:
            raise ValueError(f"Synthetic example {pdb} not in synthetic cluster file!")
        return self._synthetic_pdb_to_cluster[pdb] + num_real_clusters
    self.synthetic_csv['cluster'] = self.synthetic_csv['pdb_name'].map(synthetic_cluster_lookup)

    metadata_csv = pd.concat([metadata_csv, self.synthetic_csv])
findings.claim: With use_synthetic:True (datasets.yaml:27, on for pdb_codesign training), the entire synthetic_csv (./metadata/distillation_metadata.csv) is concatenated into the training set with no length/quality filter (pdb_filter_metadata only filters the real raw_csv). That file has 6550 rows. Replicating the real-set filters (check_train_counts.py) yields 18684 real proteins pre-redesign (matching the paper exactly) but 16313 after the use_redesigned best_rmsd<2.0 merge.
findings.concern: Sec 6.2 states 'we needed to add only an extra 4179 examples to the original set of 18684 proteins'; the released distillation set actually adds 6550 (and the redesign step drops the real set to 16313), so the paper's stated distillation composition does not match the shipped data — undercutting the 'only 4179 extra' efficiency claim, even though the two decompositions happen to share the same 22863 total.
findings.resolution: Authors: clarify whether 4179 counts examples, clusters, or an earlier distillation round, and reconcile it with the 6550-row distillation_metadata.csv actually consumed by use_synthetic (and the 16313 real examples after use_redesigned).
